6ed98fb121a6.title: Glossary: Skills
6ed98fb121a6.content: Candidate terms extracted from every skill’s front matter: name as the label, description as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 13 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 3 (SKOS) · cat-harness 246 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 19 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 46 (SKOS). Size: this page holds 327 terms and is 252 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 361 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 361 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 327 shown . Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/activity-log.md . adjudication candidate, extracted Settle a review that reached no mechanical or consensus agreement. What makes a disagreement adjudicable, the shape its implementations share, why the adjudication LEADS the criterion while the checker's entry is kept beneath it, and the dispensation that records the reason — scoped to a version, never precedent. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/adjudication.md . adopt-methodology-from-source candidate, extracted The general process for turning a shared paper, book or standard into an adopted methodology: establish origin and licence, ingest the source, find and summarize related work items and issues and ask whether to coordinate, render the method with its adopted and refused parts, place it by ownership, integrate it by calling existing processes, give every tool it uses a Tool node, and put it to the owner. Process: library/processes/methodology-from-source.bpmn. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/adopt-methodology-from-source.md . adversarial-code-review candidate, extracted Review a pull request an agent touched by building the strongest case that it is wrong, unsafe, or not what it claims, and record the verdict where the merge gate reads it: one merge-review/v1 file per head, on the merge-reviews state branch, never in the pull request itself. Covers who may review, what the whole-diff scope is, the RED FLAG categories and their evidence rule, the one rebuttal round, overrides, and how a per-head verdict composes with a merge train. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/adversarial-code-review.md . agent-handoff candidate, extracted Governs handing ONE task to an agent in another environment — a local agent with network the cloud session lacks, a sibling on a different machine, anything that cannot read the coordinator's context and that a person may relay to. States who writes which work item, where the receiver reports, what the person pastes (one sentence: work item, branch, repository) and the brief the work item opens with (second person, to the executor), what the receiver checks before acting, who closes, who may grant an exception, and how to recognise and answer the five ways an executor fails. Use when writing a work item for another agent to execute, and as the receiver before acting on one. Triggers on: hand off, handoff, local agent, agy, mac agent, needs network, executor failed, agent went silent, re-hand, "give me a branch and bean for them", relay, the other agent. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/agent-handoff.md . agent-memory candidate, extracted Durable memory for a subagent — the three entry labels and what each promises, why entries are authored as graph nodes rather than in the generated file, the injection budget that silently truncates, and archiving as the third state between "reaches everybody" and "deleted". Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/agent-memory.md . agent-permissions candidate, extracted Securing what a coding agent may do without asking, from the person who can grant it: the secure-agent-permissions sub-process, run at session start and on demand when an action is denied. Vendor-neutral: the coding agent is a Tool (Claude Code is one; Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and Codex are others), and each Tool's own config format belongs to its adapter, not here. Covers the permissions the harness's processes need, least privilege, how each one is explained before it is granted, how a grant is recorded, and the rules that no grant relaxes: never self-granted, generated projections are CI's, and merging to main is never a standing permission. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/agent-permissions.md . archimate-models candidate, extracted ArchiMate models as knowledge-graph content: how a layer declares the Archi models it holds, what the archimate subgraph gives every model, view, element and relationship (an IRI, a thin page, and every view drawn as SVG from the model's own diagram, and its metamodel derived and checked), how to version the models, how to wire them into a folio's staging build and navbar, how to count and lower the crossed lines in a view before committing it, why every view carries a plain-language key, why names are the source's own terms linked to their SKOS concepts, and why no Java, no Archi CLI and no Archi HTML report is ever part of the pipeline. Read before adding, authoring, publishing or rendering an .archimate file, before citing an ArchiMate element from prose, and before reaching for Archi's own tooling in CI. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/archimate-models.md . archiving-arxiv candidate, extracted Materializing a paper from arXiv — why the version suffix is part of the identity rather than a detail, what to keep beside the PDF, and which facts must be read from the published API rather than recalled. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/artefact-reachability.md . ask-the-person candidate, extracted Put one question or decision to a person: the full question, context and every option written in the chat FIRST, then the same options as a tappable card. Input is the composed question; output is the answer, or the default taken. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/ask-the-person.md . asset-extraction candidate, extracted Reading a container — a zip, a PDF, a saved web page — into the knowledge graph. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/skills/library-core/asset-extraction.md . associate-harness candidate, extracted Declare a harness this one knows about and does not hold (associatedHarnesses): a folio in another repository, published at its own site. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/audit-coverage.md . auto-docs candidate, extracted Derived documentation for a sub-graph — what the handler emits, what it deliberately does not, and the obligation on whoever authors a harness's docs: summarise what the index lists, by reusing it rather than restating it. 906c5c9ef99e.title: C
906c5c9ef99e.content: cache-first-ci candidate, extracted Every CI step is a pure function of its inputs: derive the inputs, hash them into a key, restore on a hit, run and save on a miss. Read before adding a cache to a workflow, before writing a cache key, before trusting a restored output or a skipped verdict, and before pushing a change that moves a cached step's key. Covers the one primitive (cached-step + cache:key), the trust classes, what a committer publishes, the 10 GB budget, and the hit-rate report. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/cache-first-ci.md . canonical-watcher candidate, extracted Derivation-discipline integration watcher — watches the default branch + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for non-canonical empirical / fitting / calibration inputs beyond the project's declared set, numerology, or justification/rationalization in place of derivation. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake, post-completion one-voice, sibling-PR comment protocol, backlog-found PR spin-up, handover docs) from sdlc-core/integration-watcher. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/spec-kit/change-size.md . ci-health candidate, extracted A red workflow looks exactly like a green one from inside a checkout. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/prepare-merge-auto.md . process-state candidate, extracted Track where you are inside a running process — which task, in which swimlane, under which role — and recover deliberately when you find yourself outside it. 59ac1171f1b3.title: R
59ac1171f1b3.content: raci candidate, extracted RACI over this repository's processes — who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for each activity. Three declared edge kinds over the roles and BPMN activities that already exist, not a new party registry. Use it to work out involvement when a project is initiated, and to sketch its breakdown. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/raci/raci.md . readme-sections candidate, extracted A folio's README is the author's file; the platform owns only the marked regions it generates. How the sync/audit split works, why the platform never generates a folio's prose, and the third state both tools must report. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/readme-sections.md . ref-stewardship candidate, extracted Steward a WATCHED REF — a long-lived branch many processes write and one consumer serialises. Covers what makes a ref need a steward at all, why a coalescing window is a different object from a hold, the four durable fields a window needs so a handover cannot double-push, and the rule that a steward stores decisions and reads facts live. Use for "gh-pages is cancelling its own deployments", "two sessions pushed the same store branch", "who owns writes to this branch", "coalesce these pushes", and before giving any ref a concurrency policy. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/ref-stewardship.md . registry-authority-contract candidate, extracted The contract the external-registry role is held to when a candidate source is checked against the body that publishes it: resolve the identifier through its own API and return the record, so authority is a resolved fact. When the answer is uncertain or absent the verdict is not invented here; the work plan records the citation as unverified. A role played by an external party is held to a contract, not handed instructions. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/content/content-lifecycle-ext/registry-authority-contract.md . related-work-coordination candidate, extracted Before new work takes shape, find the work it touches. Search work items, issues and open PRs for relevance; categorize and summarize every hit; then ask the user whether and how to coordinate. Judgement decides the categories and the recommendation, and the user decides the coordination. Called by CRDM when a requirement is initiated or updated in chat, and by methodology adoption. Process: processes/process/related-work.bpmn. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/related-work-coordination.md . release-epic-planning candidate, extracted Plan and track releases using work item epics. Covers epic creation, story/task decomposition, release readiness tracking, and the relationship between epics and GitHub milestones. Applies to code releases, paper publications, and project milestones. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/release-epic-planning.md . release-lifecycle candidate, extracted Governs the release lifecycle: semver policy, draft/named releases, changelogs, release gating, and the relationship between feature branches, PRs, work items, and releases. Applies to code releases, paper publications, and project milestones. Complements package-release (which handles the mechanics of cutting a release) with the process and policy layer. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/release-lifecycle.md . remote-mount candidate, extracted Bring a harness, and every layer it depends on, into a checkout that does not hold it, from another repository at a pinned commit, as declared directories with a lock: a source.remote entry in the downstream's root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts on its declaration) and mountDefaults on the harness. Covers when to mount and when to subscribe instead, why there are no submodules and no .deps/, the transitive closure through needs and gitlinks, overrides by id, the lock, and the three states. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/remote-mount.md . render-kg-to-cdn candidate, extracted Render a Knowledge Graph, or a list of its Subgraphs, for publication to a CDN at a publication root URL, and report a status and one message. The same step for a staging preview and for a release — only the root URL and the target differ. Names the target's Tool, never its steps: GitHub Pages (gh-pages) is one Tool, and it carries its own subprocess. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/render-kg-to-cdn.md . render-kg-to-github-pages candidate, extracted Render a Knowledge Graph, or a list of its Subgraphs, to GitHub Pages at a publication root URL, and report the push: a status (pushed, not pushed, could not determine) and one message carrying the deployed commit and the QA result. The same steps for a staging preview and for a release; only the root URL differs. Skills of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/skills/render-kg-to-github-pages.md . render-logging candidate, extracted Log every render to the publish branch — what was published, removed, restored or deliberately retained — to an append-only log that lives beside what it describes. Use when adding or removing anything on gh-pages, when asking "what happened to this preview", or before writing a workflow step that deletes a published artefact. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/render-logging.md . render-order candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/render-order.md . rendered-impact candidate, extracted The list of rendered files a Change Set alters, and how a reviewer approves against it. Each renderer maps the input files a change touched to the rendered files of its site through its dependency cone, before any build; a build diff then confirms the prediction. Use when opening or reviewing a Change Set PR, when asked "which pages does this change", when a prediction and a build disagree, or when adding a renderer. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/rendered-impact.md . rendered-verification candidate, extracted Confirm a UI change by LOOKING at it in a browser and sending the screenshots to the author, rather than describing it. Use whenever a change touches CSS, a Liquid/HTML template, a generated page, the navbar, a board, a sticky or any rendered surface — before claiming it works, and before asking the author to review it. Covers building the site locally, taking the REAL CI build off gh-pages when the question is theme chrome or layout, driving it with Playwright in this environment, measuring computed style rather than reading the stylesheet, hit-testing a control's centre because visible is not usable, asserting the conditions so a check cannot pass over an unstyled page, and the defect classes that are invisible to a green gate set. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/rendered-verification.md . repo-conversion candidate, extracted Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, scans outside the content tree for mathematical evidence and refutations, lists the content markers (an IG, a DAK, processes, work items, library, Lean, folio manifests) the harness could declare and declares only the ones the person picks, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along, or asks what else in a repository an existing harness could declare. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/repo-conversion.md . requirement-definition candidate, extracted What a requirement IS, said once for both requirements methodologies: a statement, a conformance level, a source, at least one success criterion with its verification method, and a sign-off owner. How that maps onto the req: schema's successCriteria, onto CRDM's REQ-### and spec-kit's FR/SC, and why a work plan is beans whose ## Done when is copied from the success criteria of the statements they name. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/content/requirements-planning/requirement-definition.md . retry-backoff candidate, extracted Every error gets a falling-off retry rate — each wait doubles, with jitter. Read before writing any call that can fail transiently, and before deciding that a failure is worth retrying at all. Exhausting the retries does not change the verdict. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/conduct-core/retry-backoff.md . review candidate, extracted Where to start when a person or an agent reviews a document folio larger than one chapter, such as a DAK or an L1 digital transformation handbook. A pointer, not a method: it names the review skills that already exist, says which question each one answers, and gives the order to read them in. Use when someone asks "how do I review this", when a review session starts on a large folio, or before writing a new review skill, so it is not written twice. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/review/review.md . review-comments candidate, extracted Reviewer comments on a folio's edit-set, from a tagged pull-request comment to a structured todo on the review page. Covers the tag a reviewer types, how the comments are ingested into review-comment/1.0.0 todos, where the published review-comments.json comes from and when it refreshes, how a comment follows a renamed block and survives a removed one, who may change a comment's status, and how to change this process. Use when a reviewer asks how to comment on a block, when the review page shows no comments or a wrong one, when editing the ingestion, or when a folio's staging workflow is set up. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/content/content-lifecycle-ext/review-comments.md . review-heatmap candidate, extracted The review page's heat map: a section-by-metric table that tells a reviewer of a large document where to look first. Says what each column MEANS and what it must NOT be read as, where each number comes from, what a column says when a build lacks its data, and how the colour was chosen. Use when a reviewer or author asks "where do I start", reads a number off the heat map, or asks why coverage or QA say "no data"; and before adding a column. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/authoring/authoring-core/review-heatmap.md . review-log-watch candidate, extracted Poll a review log (a drafting Contributor Feedback sheet, or a public-comment sheet's Review Change Sets) and its folio repository's issues mechanically, with Tool review-log-watch, and start agent work only when a cell people set or an open issue changed. Each issue that no row links yet becomes a Contributor Feedback row, and a closed issue's row is hidden with its text struck through. Use on every wake of a review-log watcher, and when setting up a watcher for a new log. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/content/folio-document-adapter/review-log-watch.md . review-sheet-agent-columns candidate, extracted Whenever an agent works on a change set of a folio whose review sheet is kept by the Tool review-sheet-sync, it writes the Agent tabs' columns for that change set and its comments as it goes: status, step, what it did, the PR, the staging page and its build, what the PR changed and when it finished. Use on every change-set edit, draft, PR, push, merge or close, in a sheet sync or not. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/content/folio-document-adapter/review-sheet-agent-columns.md . review-sheet-script candidate, extracted Build, install and reuse the Google Apps Script that keeps a review sheet's links and joined columns current (Tool review-sheet-sync). Public-comment mode: comment numbers, sections, pages and lines link into the frozen review draft, and Review Change Sets joins its comments. Drafting mode: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set with its own GitHub issue, and Sections pick from the document's table of contents. Use when setting up either sheet for a document, when its links are missing or stale, or after a tab, header, anchor or draft link changes. Skills of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/skills/content/folio-document-adapter/review-sheet-script.md . role-model candidate, extracted Actors, roles and skills — who performs a BPMN task, under which swimlane, with which skills. How a role's skill set is resolved through inherits and through a subprocess call chain, how a lane binds to a declared role, and how kg:audit finds a dangling skill, lane, role or decision. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/role-model.md . root-readme candidate, extracted Write the repository's root README when there is none, carrying a link to the harness that was installed and the overall install status. Never replaces one that exists. It runs only once the install has succeeded. Skills of bootstrap · source bootstrap/skills/root-readme.md .

25bf90647d42.content: sample-import candidate, extracted Testing an import of a SAMPLE of a remote source into a knowledge graph or other structured store: scope it, let materialize-remote gate it, land it in the library (permanent) or the kept, unpublished trashcan (trial), import it, and test the import. The gates are called, never copied. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/skills/large-datasets/sample-import.md . saturation-meta-merge candidate, extracted When the CI runners have been full for a long time, drain a repository's ready PRs in one step: hold the swarm, cancel the queued PR runs, stack every admitted PR onto one meta-merge branch with merge commits, and land that branch on main without waiting for CI, on the owner's card that names each PR. Then re-run main's checks and report. Use for "runners are full", "cancel everything and merge what's ready", "meta-merge", "consolidate the queue", and when the queue has not moved for an hour or more. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/saturation-meta-merge.md . schema-management candidate, extracted Manage a schema over its life — add one, change one, read the schema graph and its viewer, and act on what the reader could not determine. The layout rule lives in directory-conventions; the entity question lives in data-modelling; this is the work in between. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/schema-management.md . scientific-accuracy candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/authoring/authoring-core/scientific-accuracy.md . secrets candidate, extracted Adding, rotating and revoking the credentials the harness's automation needs, one mechanism at a time, with the exact GitHub UI path for each step. Every step that touches a value is a person's; an agent drafts the steps, checks names and expiry dates, and records what was done. Leads with the GitHub App on a personal account, the recommended mechanism. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/secrets.md . security candidate, extracted The security sub-KG's entry point. What the boundaries are, which machinery already guards each one, and the single rule that unifies them — refuse, never repair. Read this before adding a check, so the answer that already exists is reused rather than rebuilt in a fourth place. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/conduct/security/security.md . serving-renderings candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/serving-renderings.md . session-context candidate, extracted What a state machine tracks across a session, as against one process instance. What the record carries, why actor is required and the rest are not, why the session's view of a node is advisory, and what a sibling session reads it for. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/session-context.md . session-intent candidate, extracted Session-start intent declaration + session-end results recording, against the work plan's goals (milestone work items) and their open work items. Enforces the durable-handoff discipline so any agent can pick up another's thread. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/session-intent.md . session-state-machine candidate, extracted An agent PLAYING a state machine rather than an engine executing one. Where the non-determinism actually lives, why the diagram stays strict, the cat-harness.processes:judgement marker that makes a judgement point countable, and what the machine must never do on the actor's behalf. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/session-state-machine.md . signing candidate, extracted What any signature in the harness must answer, whatever it covers: who signs, what bytes are signed, which signature suites are accepted and who decides that, where the key is kept, which route signs (API or person, by reach), and what a verifier must check and record. Suites are named by the identifiers the standards already define. Signing is done by the parties' own systems; the harness verifies. Read before you add a signature slot, a trust anchor, a verifier, or a process that signs anything. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/signing.md . site-presentation-assets candidate, extracted A visual fact — a colour, a glyph, a theme — lives in a graph node, and the stylesheet the site serves is a rendering of it. Read before adding a colour, an icon or a theme, before hand-editing any generated stylesheet, and before referencing a generated asset from a page. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/theming/site-presentation-assets.md . skill-registration candidate, extracted Adding a skill is never a one-file change. What a new skill file owes, the one command that performs the derived half, the one declaration it deliberately leaves to you, why running it once is not enough, and the two orphan directions it reports rather than fixes. Read this before adding, renaming or removing a skill. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/skill-registration.md . skill-voice-review candidate, extracted Reviews a skill against a voice that judges skills — the base agent-skill-authoring voice or a vendor override such as Claude's, Gemini CLI's or OpenAI's — rule by rule, with each rule's citation open, and records the verdicts with voice:review. Use when skill-voice-review-current reports a skill never reviewed or reviewed before the skill or the voice changed, or when asked whether a skill follows a vendor's authoring guidance. The agent half of that axis; the mechanical half, in scripts/skill-voice-review.ts, only says whether a current review exists. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/skill-voice-review.md . skills-and-tools candidate, extracted A skill states a capability generically; a Tool node carries the concrete mechanism. Read before writing or editing any skill, and whenever a skill is about to name a vendor, a CLI, a binary or an API endpoint. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/tools/folio-core/skills-and-tools.md . smart-launch candidate, extracted How a browser app performs a SMART on FHIR launch — EHR launch and standalone launch — with the SMARTerFHIR library: SmartLaunchHandler, the LAUNCH and EMR enums, the scopes it requests per EHR vendor, how the redirect URI is computed, and where the token ends up. Written against a pinned upstream commit; read before wiring a launch page or a redirect page. Skills of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/skills/fhir-client/smart-launch.md . spec-kit candidate, extracted Spec-driven development, adopted whole: define what and why before deciding how, and do not develop before a spec exists. Carries what this platform adopts and — separately, with reasons — what it refuses. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/spec-kit/spec-kit.md . spec-template candidate, extracted The single declared template artefact for platform feature specifications, adopted from github/spec-kit. Mandatory sections and required fields are machine-readable here for automated validation. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/spec-kit/spec-template.md . specification-compiled-agents candidate, extracted When a diagram already says what the process is, the model should not be planning it. The two gaps between this repository's engine and a compiled control plane — typed node contracts and per-node context scope — what to do before either exists, and the three things not to adopt with the method. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/workflow/specification-compiled-agents.md . specification-management candidate, extracted Governs the lifecycle, syntax, and traceability of specifications and requirements across the harness. Connects spec-kit and CRDM tracks to the 6-part bootstrap Requirement definition, enforces EARS and ISO 29148 statement quality, and defines how requirements project to open standards (ReqIF, OSLC-RM) while keeping bootstrap strictly decoupled. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/specification-management.md . staging-review candidate, extracted Staging preview and before/after comparison for content review. Takes one optional string — what the reader wants to look at, in their own words — and returns a list of URLs, each looked up in the publish ref, with what is published at it and what to review there. Provides before (MAIN) and after (branches/) pairs so reviewers can compare rather than guess. Used by the CRDM feature development workflow, content authoring review sessions, and whenever a staging preview deploys or someone asks to see it. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/ui/ui-core/staging-review.md . stalled-agent-triage candidate, extracted Triage incoming work from stalled agents. Given named agents or sessions, or a time window, find what they left (handover reports, open PRs, branches, work items, issue and PR discussions, workflow instances), collect as many handover reports as exist, reconstruct the rest, consolidate the workstreams into 2–4 themes, recommend how to fold them into the current or a new work plan, and coordinate open PRs with their owners (the merge steward above all). Use when a session or a swarm has stalled, timed out or lost its container, or when the owner says "pick up what X was doing". Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/stalled-agent-triage.md . sub-kg-lifecycle candidate, extracted A sub-KG is a knowledge graph staged as a directory inside a harnessed repository, declared as its own layer, that may later leave for a repository of its own. The lifecycle: declare it in place, grow it, stage it for separation (one import seam, the separation guard, a self-contained rehearsal), and then, each behind an explicit owner confirmation, create the repository, copy the staged contents in with history, re-point the declaration, verify on a fresh clone and delete the in-repo copy. The light sibling of kg-separation: use this for a DATA layer that leaves whole, and kg-separation when a graph must split into a content repository and a tools repository. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/graph-management/sub-kg-lifecycle.md . surprise-to-corpus candidate, extracted What was unexpected in that task, and does it belong in the corpus? Logical surprise is the detectable kind, recurrence is the filter that stops this generating noise every turn, and the agent PROMPTS — it never writes corpus guidance unasked. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/surprise-to-corpus.md . swarm-management candidate, extracted Decide whether to run parallel agents at all, and if so how many, at which model level, against which decomposition. Read BEFORE dispatching more than one background agent — a swarm spends the author's tokens and the decision is theirs. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/skills/sdlc-core/swarm-management.md . swimlane-glossary candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/swimlane-glossary.md . swot-analysis candidate, extracted Running a SWOT situation analysis — the activities of swot-analysis.bpmn, what each step must produce, and the one thing the technique must never be used for. The method itself lives in the methodology graph and is not repeated here. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/process/process-core/swot-analysis.md . symbiotic-interaction candidate, extracted Recognize and respond to the three epistemic registers of author input — Socratic steer (known-answer correction), honest gap (flagged unknown), and intuition seed (tenuous cross-domain identification) — with the coactive-learning measurement spec (per-arc correction quality and turns-to-convergence) and the prompt-lexicon convention. Carries the STRICT rule that a steer correcting a RULE is written into the skill that governs it, in the same turn, quoted and dated — use whenever the author corrects, settles or overrules anything. 610a6746655b.title: Glossary: Schema fields, T–Z
610a6746655b.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. ffcc3da1b769.title: Glossary: Schema fields, F–L
ffcc3da1b769.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2572 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 180 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 208 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 630 terms and is 371 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 630 shown . F G H I J K L

5baa1d0406d2.title: Glossary: Schema fields, D–E
5baa1d0406d2.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2572 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 180 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 208 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 214 terms and is 127 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 214 shown . D E

Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2572 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 180 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 208 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 270 terms and is 156 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. 70ba186de9fc.title: Glossary: Schema fields, A–C
70ba186de9fc.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2572 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 180 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 208 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 542 terms and is 325 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 542 shown . A B C

9245843ffb2e.title: Glossary: Schema fields, M–O
9245843ffb2e.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 45 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2572 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 180 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 208 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 234 terms and is 141 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2860 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 234 shown . M N O

e9e3a82da0e0.title: public health
e9e3a82da0e0.content: A guideline whose recommendations address the health of populations rather than of an individual patient: prevention, health promotion, immunization and screening programmes, surveillance, and policy or environmental measures. Also called: public health guideline . Looked up against the MeSH RDF API (id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/, 2026-10-23): closeMatch to MeSH D011634 ('Public Health', Topical Descriptor) and D015980 ('Public Health Practice', Topical Descriptor). Recorded as closeMatch rather than exactMatch because this concept classifies a guideline's domain rather than the field of public health itself.

c659dad37357.title: clinical
c659dad37357.content: A guideline whose recommendations address the care of individual patients by health workers: assessment, diagnosis, treatment and management of a condition in a person. Also called: clinical guideline, clinical health . Looked up against the MeSH RDF API (id.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/, 2026-10-23): closeMatch to MeSH D017065 ('Practice Guideline', Publication Type; entry terms 'Clinical Guideline', 'Clinical Practice Guideline') and D015510 ('Clinical Medicine', Topical Descriptor). Neither is an exactMatch because this concept classifies a guideline's domain within a three-way partition (clinical, public health, health system strengthening) rather than publication form or the medical discipline as a whole.

8a4042a65339.title: health system strengthening
8a4042a65339.content: A guideline whose recommendations address how the health system itself is organised and resourced — service delivery, health workforce, health information systems, access to medical products, financing, and leadership and governance — rather than a particular condition or population intervention. Also called: health systems strengthening, HSS . The six areas follow WHO's health-system building blocks (Everybody's business, 2007). 6a2d03f722c3.title: H
6a2d03f722c3.content: health system strengthening A guideline whose recommendations address how the health system itself is organised and resourced — service delivery, health workforce, health information systems, access to medical products, financing, and leadership and governance — rather than a particular condition or population intervention. 6c0901921985.title: P
6c0901921985.content: public health A guideline whose recommendations address the health of populations rather than of an individual patient: prevention, health promotion, immunization and screening programmes, surveillance, and policy or environmental measures. Build an IG repository's own site from its cached AST, with no instance declaration candidate, extracted The three checkout scripts the platform's site build runs for a repository that holds an IG and only mounts layers (index.config.json): ig-site:ast restores the AST from the IG's cache branch (ig-cache.sh restore) and judges it, refusing a stale, cannot-tell or absent one (a stale one is accepted for a preview by default, refused with SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=0, and never accepted for the root); ig-site:compose derives the artefact index from the AST (binding any IG API sidecars a layer above left in $SITE_WORK/ig-api/), writes the thin artefact pages, stages the IG's input/ and sushi-config.yaml (menu read at build time, palette from the webpage theme of the top layer the repository mounts, edit links from its origin) and composes it at the ROOT of the host site source; ig-site:publisher-pages serves each of the AST's resources once, as <Type>-<id>.json at the root (no ast-data/ mirror) — reduced (minified, no narrative, no ELM data, the ELM attachment pointing at the full copy) when the pages read the full resources by raw URL from the AST cache commit, and off with SITE_ROOT_RESOURCES=0 — the artefact index (or fhir-artifact-index/index.ref.json, pointing at the cache's copy) and the sidecars (or none, read from the cache), refuses a page wearing the IG Publisher's chrome, repairs repeated element ids and stamps folio-build.json. Never runs the Publisher and never reads its output. Check a review log and its repository's issues for changes candidate, extracted The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet's Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository's open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled no-sheet and, with --author, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check's. Unchanged: it prints {"status":"unchanged"} and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell's old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet (Title the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): first paragraph, Issue the issue's URL; a closed issue's row marked closed), and closedRows, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log's Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled change-set unless --label says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an issue-unlinked change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With --accept it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against. ef9520cd26d2.content: WHO SMART Guidelines approach chart candidate, extracted Draw the WHO SMART Guidelines approach chart (knowledge layers L1–L5 with their products, and their country adaptations, between the research, localisation and impact bands) as SVG from smart-guidelines-approach-figure/v1 data on a who-iris library entry, such as the product catalogue handbook's Fig. 5. bd6a03228c1f.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, R–Z
bd6a03228c1f.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 639 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 229 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 367 terms and is 310 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 367 shown . R S T U V W

cf0d8dd6bd69.title: R
cf0d8dd6bd69.content: Raise a finding against the wrong side candidate, extracted The prose and the code really disagree: raise a finding that names which side is wrong and why. Usually the prose, because the code is what runs — but a skill can state intended behaviour correctly while the code has regressed, and then the finding is against the code. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/narrative-code-review.bpmn#A_RaiseFinding . Raise findings before the assets land candidate, extracted Findings go back to whoever authored the choice, because the choice was theirs: a theme is picked per note by a human or an agent, and there is no mapping to correct instead. Raised, never silently fixed — a reviewer who re-themes a note has substituted their judgement for the author's without saying so. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_RaiseFindings . Raise the window the reader selected candidate, extracted Raise the selected window to the top. Selecting ANY part raises it, not just a title bar. Z-order is session-only by stated default: no z is written to the layout, so a raise is never a file write. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-open-close.bpmn#A_Raise . Re-enter a train on the new head candidate, extracted The next train is the verifier: the executor's own log is evidence, not the close. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_Retrain . Re-evaluate liveness AT REMOVAL TIME candidate, extracted Re-evaluated AT REMOVAL TIME, through the same previewLiveness the health sweep uses rather than a second implementation of it. The sweep runs daily and proposes; this acts. Between them a branch can come back to life — bean w2g5 documents exactly that, a session reusing one branch across five successive pull requests. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_Preflight . Re-execute a sample, blind to the tester's verdicts candidate, extracted Given the plan, the bound data and a sample of case ids — not the report. Says agree, disagree or unknown; unknown (could not run) is said as plainly as a disagreement, because the table reads both the same way and an unknown read as agreement certifies on one party's word. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/test-plan-execution.bpmn#A_ReExecuteSample . Re-materialize and record new fixity candidate, extracted The gates are re-asked, not inherited: a licence can change, and a collection can grow past the size a caller agreed to. AND THE NEW FIXITY IS RECORDED IN THE SAME CHANGE. This step rewrites bytes that a materialization record describes, so leaving the old digest behind would make a CORRECT run of this process fail check:materialized-fixity as a mismatch — the gate reading "somebody edited held content without saying so" about the one process whose job is to replace it. This is the publication exception, stated as a rule rather than as a carve-out, because a list of permitted writers goes stale when a writer is added. The exception is NOT "these actors may skip the rule"; it is "say what you did". A writer that updates the digest alongside the bytes passes, and the record then describes what is actually there. A writer that does not fails, correctly, because it has forked upstream silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Apply . Re-pin downstream mounts, as PRs candidate, extracted For each layer whose index.config.json mounts this repository: a PR moving ref to the merge commit, with a trust.consent whose evidence quotes the owner's consent to that pin, and the lock regenerated by mount:remote. Each re-pin PR is itself a merge to main and runs this process again. When the re-pin moves a layer whose software-library nodes are derived at the pin (bootstrap-tools, whose nodes cat-harness-tools holds in libraries/held/), the same PR runs bun run cat libraries:derive, and libraries:check fails until it does (owner, 2026-10-30, bootstrap-tools#44). None found is recorded with where it looked. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_Repin . Re-point: livesAt, seam, mount or subscription candidate, extracted In the new repository livesAt goes (absent means it sits at the root of repository) and platform.ts points at where the platform now is. The host consumes it as a remote mount (a source.remote instance in its root index.config.json) if it imports its code, or a subscription if it only reads its content, pinned to a commit while staging. Additive: the host keeps its copy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-move.bpmn#Task_Repoint . Re-read the prose against the code candidate, extracted For each open item, read the prose claim beside the code it describes and decide what is true. For a stale pair, read what changed in the code and whether the prose still describes it. For an undetermined claim, say whether it points at something real outside this repository. For a false claim, check the checker's reading before trusting it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/narrative-code-review.bpmn#A_ReRead . Re-render the agent surface candidate, extracted When the lock changed, the layers an agent's skills and memory are generated from changed with it. mount:remote re-runs the generators of what an agent actually reads — skill:commands (.claude/commands/) and agent-memory (.claude/agent-memory/ and the .agents/ copies) — from the checkout root, and a generator that fails fails the run. A re-pin commit therefore carries the new layers AND the surface rendered from them, because new layers shipped without their rendered surface fail the agent-memory tests. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Render . Moves the change-set to another TWG review committee and records who, when, from, to and why on the change-set record, so re-ingesting comments never resets it. Not drift: synonyms, articles, word order, inflection, a purpose clause rendered in the subjunctive, an acronym left uninflected, an acronym spelled out with the acronym kept. Sign the package and/or each asset candidate, extracted THE TRUST ANCHOR IS GDHCN, SPECIFIED BY THE WHO SMART TRUST IG. READ OFF THAT IG rather than from general knowledge: a GDHCN trustlist distributes KEY MATERIAL as W3C DID documents, and says nothing about what you wrap your bytes in — the health-certificate envelope is a separate specification in the same IG, and a document package is not a health certificate. So what is settled is where a verifier GETS THE KEY, not what it verifies. A portal that can fetch the bytes but not reach the trustlist cannot verify, which is unknown and not a failure — air-gapped is a declared deployment value, so that case is answered rather than assumed away. Still OPEN and unread: the rotation and revocation model, and whether a document-package signature can be expressed for a GDHCN-aware verifier at all. Two schemes with different properties remain to choose between, and the trustlist does not choose between them. A PACKAGE signature over the manifest verifies the SET — nothing added, removed or altered — and must be reissued whenever any file changes. A PER-ASSET signature verifies one file independently, which is what an edge cache serving one asset can actually check, and it cannot detect a removal because there is nothing left to verify. They compose; composing them is the safer and more expensive default, and it is the deployment's choice rather than the pipeline's. (NOT A GATE) candidate, extracted Bean qbco, issue #2456 (owner, 2026-10-07: "1y, 2y, 3y, 4y"). On a PUSH to main only; on any other event it is skipped and nothing waits for it. A merge-button merge of an up-to-date PR carries a tree CI has already tested. verdict-reuse.sh looks up the runs of this workflow on the merged head (the merge commit's second parent) and answers reuse=true only when one concluded success, ran every job a reuse would skip, and tested exactly this tree: for a pull_request run, the tested-tree: its Task_QaWorkingCopy job wrote into its check run's summary; for a dispatch, the head's own tree. Then the four bun test shards (part of Task_TypeScript), the three e2e shards (Task_E2E) and the standalone ratchet (part of Task_RepositoryGates) are skipped on this push, and the summary names the run whose verdict stands. Everything that judges the tree against main or reads qa-reports still runs. A squash, an API error, a missing record or a mismatch is reuse=false and every job runs: could-not-determine is never green. Drawn before the fork because the jobs it can skip wait for it; the others do not. Since the same ruling, a newer push to main also cancels an older main run still in progress (the workflow's concurrency), so main's verdict history is thinned by decision. 2a9914750fe5.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, A–D
2a9914750fe5.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 639 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 229 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 294 terms and is 246 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 294 shown . 0–9 A B C D

72c6ad930796.content: 1 · Declare in place (nothing moves) candidate, extracted A <name>.json entry with its graphs[] kinds. A sub-graph that owns its own layout gains a NESTED declaration whose paths resolve against its own directory, so the whole graph relocates by moving one folder. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Declare . 2a · Measure — unassigned column FIRST candidate, extracted bun run cat check:partition. Read the unassigned column before the edge count, and quote BOTH numbers rather than only the one that improved. The edge count can rise when the measurement improves (previously unjudged edges are folded in); that is correct. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Measure . 2b · Prune, merge, factor — or the classification is wrong candidate, extracted The only four moves. Move the shared TARGET first and the importers after; check the target's layer before the importer's; a schema moves with its script. The fix is never an exemption, it is the right owner. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Move . 3 · Isolate — own declaration, namespace, artefact candidate, extracted Only once cross-edges measure zero: give the sub-graph its own declaration, its own namespace and its own published artefact, as bootstrap/ has (its own declaration, bs: namespace and graph document). Nothing moves yet; the sub-graph now stands alone in place. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Isolate . 4 · Extract — a directory move, not a file-by-file sift candidate, extracted Only once edges are zero and the declaration stands alone: move the sub-graph out as one directory move, not a file-by-file sift. Its nested declaration resolves paths against its own directory, so moving the folder moves the graph. The five-point gate is in migration-plan.md Phase II. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Extract .

0d46e348f476.title: A
0d46e348f476.content: Abort, restore the tree, list what was refused candidate, extracted git merge --abort. Each refused path is listed with its pattern's reason, or "no declared pattern". BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-base.bpmn#Task_Abort . Accept it, and record where it came from candidate, extracted Both branches land here. An unprompted offer is accepted as it stands — do not make somebody follow a process to hand over what they already have. Provenance is recorded whichever channel it arrived through: a description given in chat has a source and can be wrong, exactly as a PDF does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Accept . Accept the new state candidate, extracted Runs the check again with --accept, so the state file holds what was just handled and the next poll compares against it. A row the pass could not finish stays changed and is picked up on the next poll. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_Accept . Accept, or send back candidate, extracted The editor's lane, kept separate on purpose: the reviewer who judged the change is not the position that accepts it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Accessibility: measure, do not assert candidate, extracted Contrast COMPUTED against the real ground, including the worst case a backdrop can present; a non-colour channel wherever colour carries meaning (SC 1.4.1); an accessible name on every region; keyboard and focus order. An automated pass is necessary and not sufficient — axe accepts a non-empty placeholder as an accessible name, and a CSS selector that matches nothing raises no error at all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Accessibility . Act on the answer candidate, extracted Never ask the person again for what they answered. A rule-level answer goes into the governing skill in the same turn. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Act . Add an actor, and declare its kind candidate, extracted Human, agentic or mechanical. A userTask because the agentic/mechanical line is JUDGEMENT — role-model.md says so — and reading it wrong disqualifies the actor from every judgement task it exists to perform, silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_AddActor . Address the review candidate, extracted Every finding is answered — implemented, or replied to with why not. A design question does not excuse skipping the nits in the same review. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_AddressReview . Adjudicate against the checker candidate, extracted The reviewer and a checker read the same claim differently — a disagreement about ONE kg-qa criterion (prose-claims-resolve). Descend into Process_CriterionAdjudication, which runs the shared adjudication and then one of its three outcomes: the checker's finding stands, the criterion is scoped, or a dispensation is granted with its reason. The checker's entry is kept beneath the verdict rather than overwritten (requirement R4 of issue #1042). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/narrative-code-review.bpmn#Call_Adjudication . Adjudicate the conflict candidate, extracted A human or agentic decision, never a merge rule. Which side wins depends on why the local edit was made, and a process that picked automatically would be choosing without the one fact that decides it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the criterion disagreement candidate, extracted The shared judgement — entry condition, untainted dispatch, person-or-agent restriction — asked with THIS question's permitted answers. cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes sits here rather than on A_Adjudicate inside it because the answers depend on what was asked, and the gateway below is what acts on them: the engine refuses a mismatch between the two. Process_Adjudication may also leave at End_NotAdjudicable — one entry and no other side is a review or a gate, not a disagreement — in which case nothing below runs and there is nothing to record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement candidate, extracted The judgement itself, and the one step nothing here can check: if a mechanism could decide it, the process would not have been entered. It declares NO cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on purpose, and that absence is the whole of bean bvuk. This step used to name three — stands, scope, dispensation — and six diagrams called it: review-narrative and voice-review, whose question those three answer, and four whose question they do not. refresh-materialized asks which side wins a local-vs-remote conflict; there is no criterion to scope there and no dispensation to grant, yet the outcome half ran regardless. Since the caller's question decides the permitted answers, the caller declares them: cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on its OWN call activity, with its own gateway acting on them. criterion-adjudication.bpmn is that for the QA-criterion question. What could NOT be fixed by passing the codes as data, which was this bean's first recommendation: the three branches ran three different TASKS, so a caller handed local-wins would have had it pointing at A_ScopeCriterion. The branches had to move, not the enum. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/adjudication.bpmn#A_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement candidate, extracted adjudication.bpmn. When the editor and a reviewer, or two reviewers, disagree about a finding, an adjudicator settles it and records why; the review comment moves to adjudicated with the Decision that closed it. Permitted answers: stands — the finding is right and the author addresses it; withdrawn — the finding is wrong and the comment closes. Recorded on the comment, not branched: either way the flow goes on to the coverage check. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-committee.bpmn#Call_Adjudication . Adjudicate the flagged passage candidate, extracted A machine can detect that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_FlagDrift . Adjudicate the flagged passage (human) candidate, extracted A human SME or editor reviews the flagged passage. They may: - Accept the translation as-is (false positive) - Edit the translation and re-run QA - Reject and request re-translation The round trip establishes that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the voice findings candidate, extracted Three outcomes, all legitimate: the register is wrong for this genre; the criterion does not belong in this genre and should carry profiles; or the block is a stated exception and a reviewer entry records why. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-narrative.bpmn#Task_AdjudicateVoice . Adjudicate: prose, scope, or exception candidate, extracted The same three outcomes as the base voice axis. The register is wrong for this block (fix the prose); the rule does not apply to this content (scope it on the voice, one edit rather than ten overrules); or the rule applies and this block is an exception (a reviewer entry saying why). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudication candidate, extracted folio-assistant's adjudication: the adjudication leads, the checker's entry is kept, and the dispensation carries its reason. Reviewers disagreeing on ONE criterion is a criterion disagreement, so this calls the QA-criterion specialisation: the failing entry stands, the criterion does not apply to this screen, or a dispensation is granted with its reason. The entry condition matches exactly rather than approximately: GW_Agree asks whether the blind reviewers' entries agree and takes no here, and Process_CriterionAdjudication starts at "entries for one criterion disagree" — R_Review records pass, warn or fail PER CRITERION with a reason, so the disagreement reaching this step is a per-criterion disagreement between reviewer entries and nothing else. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Admit it to the train, record the train id candidate, extracted Writes the queue entry's trainId and placement (rule, class, rank) with who decided and when. A decision, so it is stored; the facts it was decided on are not. PRECONDITION, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the worktree carries no untracked, non-ignored file before the member is merged and the tree regenerated. git status --porcelain must be empty. The reason is specific: generated directory READMEs carry a per-subdirectory file count, and the writer counts the files GIT WOULD COMMIT -- git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard (bootstrap-tools/scripts/git-files.ts:23). --exclude-standard already keeps IGNORED junk out, which is the __pycache__ case that drove that line, but --others still counts an untracked file nobody has ignored. So a transient written by an earlier train step moves a committed count, readme:subgraphs:check goes red, and the red belongs to nobody. Train 6 hit this. A PREVIEW REBUILDS ONLY ITS DEPENDENCY CONE (owner cards Q-CONE-1 C and Q-CONE-2 B, 2026-11-01): main's writer records say what each derive:publish writer and each step of the QA working copy READ. Build the entry candidate, extracted First the working copy is produced (qa:refresh, bean 3hk4): while the checkout still tracks test/results/, the commit's own copy is the record and nothing runs; once it does not, every declared QA writer runs into the empty tree, because the gates are in judge mode and wrote nothing a publish could carry. A refresh that leaves a writer failed, a family empty or a file unclaimed is INCOMPLETE: the job goes red and qa:publish --completeness refuses, so a partial tree is never stored as the commit's record — the "Not stored" outcome, reached before any push. Then it hashes the working copy of every declared qa directory (<instance>/test/results/**, byte-identical to the checkout's layout) into a tree through a private index, and writes manifest.json (qa-reports-manifest/v1): inputs, producers, verdict counts and the gates' result. Identical JSON is the same blob, so an unchanged family costs nothing to store again. Its git objects live in a private bare repository, never in the checkout's own store. A stale cache is first rebuilt incrementally (IncrementalBuildCli), falling back to a full AstExportCli build with -tx; a force run, a pre-export caller, or a missing or cannot-tell cache always builds in full, and a release needs a full build. The caller's optional pre-export overlay command runs before a full build; the inputs it changed are put back and the AST is recorded against the clean commit's input digest (ig-ast.ts source-inputs). e4cfec0847f3.content: Cancel queued PR runs; build, push, merge candidate, extracted Never cancel a main push run that has started. Open one PR per repository, merge it with a merge commit, and comment on each member PR with the link. When most pages of a document with no outline fail, the whole document is read from OCR, as for a scan. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, "A text layer that is not text". Every JSON Schema the harness publishes (its $id) and every JSON-LD document (its vocabulary, its diagram vocabulary, its graph export, each carrying its own @context) is at the address it names under iriBase, where a program following the IRI finds it. Two checks: that the site build stages each one at its address, and that each address answers. A 404 is not published; a 403 or no answer from here could not be determined. Check the selected methodology's evidence base candidate, extracted Before applying a methodology, establish that the thing being applied is what it claims to be. A methodology is adopted because it is somebody else's named, external work; this step checks that the origin it cites resolves to a source in a declared library, and reads the methodology-evidence QA sidecar for it. WHY THE CHECK IS HERE AND NOT AT ADOPTION. Adoption happens once; selection happens every time a decision is made. A source that was reachable when the methodology was adopted can stop being so, and a methodology adopted before this axis existed was never checked at all. Measured 2026-09-22: six methodologies cited an origin and NONE had that source in any library, so every selection made until then rested on an unverifiable citation. WHAT A GAP DOES AND DOES NOT DO. A missing source does NOT block the decision, and this step has no branch that stops the process — that would make a documentation gap into an outage, and the owner decides whether an unbacked methodology may still be used. "Source ingested", "source located but unreachable from here" and "no source found" are three different facts, and literature-search exists largely to stop the middle one being reported as the last.
