Moves each staged site INTO the host's Jekyll source at <instance>/, with its includes and data namespaced per IG. Pages wear the thin layout with the host's chrome linked (--full-pages inlines the host's full chrome instead). Prints one <instance> <jekyll source> <at> line per IG: the build list the host keeps (./_ig-list.txt) for the post-build pass. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/tools/ig-docs-site-compose.bpmn#Task_ComposeInto . Compose the full question candidate, extracted What is being decided, stated as what will differ; every id, path and coined name glossed; every option with its letter, a one-line explanation and its trade-off; the recommendation, first and marked; what will happen if no answer comes. Can the reader answer without opening anything? If not, it is not ready. More than one decision open: ask the next one in full and give a count for the rest. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/ask-the-person.bpmn#A_Compose . Compose the hand-back and post it in own thread candidate, extracted Compose it once, against the input schema: a question is the full ask-the-person input (what will differ, context, lettered options with a one-line trade-off each, the recommendation, what happens with no answer); context, a result or a blocker gets the same stand-alone test. Post it in your own thread too, chat text then card. Your own thread is never the only copy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Compose . Compose the message candidate, extracted Five required strings — timestamp, actor, process, task, message — and one optional markdown body. The five are required because each answers a question a reader of the log will otherwise have to guess, and a guessed answer in a log is worse than a missing one. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/log-message.bpmn#A_Compose . Compute the cone of the change candidate, extracted fsh-cone --changed (scripts/fsh-cone.ts) over the changed files: the forward cone is what to rebuild, the backward cone is what to check out. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Cone . Confirm all criteria met candidate, extracted The business analyst confirms every acceptance criterion from the requirements is met. The issue closes only on their authorisation — an agent never closes an issue on its own say-so. It IS an adjudication with the requirement-set answers: an approval here moves the set to accepted, which check:requirements refuses unless it is a human's and every approved member is in-force. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#BA_Confirm . Confirm main's CI on the merge commit candidate, extracted Read the runs on the merge commit. Red is fixed forward (continual-progress). With no CI the report reads "not verified: no CI", never green. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Task_ConfirmBase . Confirm needs statement candidate, extracted Stakeholders confirm, on the issue, that the needs statement says what they need — or say what to change. A stakeholder's judgement; an agent does not record it for them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#S_ConfirmNeeds . Confirm the cardinalities candidate, extracted An operational question, asked of the people who run the process because they know where the exceptions are. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#S_ConfirmCardinality . Confirm the entities are the ones meant candidate, extracted A naming question. The BA owns the domain vocabulary; the agent does not guess, which is CRDM's own rule for phase 1 and applies here with more force. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#BA_ConfirmEntities . Consolidate findings candidate, extracted One report from however many subprocesses ran. Findings are advice: a reviewer cannot accept the change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_Consolidate . Consolidate into 2-4 themes, with a recommendation each candidate, extracted Group by what the work delivers, not by agent. Each theme gets its epic, members, dependencies, risk, and one of: continue, fold in, new epic, park, scrap (owner only). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/stalled-agent-triage.bpmn#A_Consolidate . Contributor feedback candidate, extracted Process_ContributorFeedback: while the document is a working draft, the Authoring Committee gives feedback through the Contributor Feedback sheet, and each change set is edited and merged in its own pull request. When its changes are merged, the document is validated and rendered again. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/folio-review-publish.bpmn#Call_ContributorFeedback . Coordinate? How? candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/related-work.bpmn#U_Coordinate . Copy asset into target folio and declare in assets[] candidate, extracted Write the asset bytes into a declared path inside the target folio and add the KgAsset entry to the target folio's <name>.json assets[] list (directory-conventions). Never drop the copy into an undeclared scratch directory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/copy-into-folio.bpmn#Task_CopyAndDeclareAsset . Create feature branch candidate, extracted Agent creates a feature branch from main. Branch naming: feature/<short-description> Opens a PR immediately (AGENTS.md: "open the PR at the first commit"). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_CreateBranch . Create the bean (agent CLI, not an engine op) candidate, extracted beans create "<title>". This is the AGENT's call. The workflow engine has no create op — its vocabulary is claim, note, resolve and archive, all of which act on an instance's existing bean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/bean-open.bpmn#Open_Create . Create the repositories candidate, extracted The owner creates the content and tools repositories and their Pages. Nothing is committed to them before this. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-move.bpmn#Task_Create . Create the repository candidate, extracted Only on the new-repo branch, and only after the user has named it. An empty working directory is scaffolded in place instead. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_CreateRepo . Cross the axes into SO, WO, ST, WT candidate, extracted The TOWS matching step, and the only step that produces anything actionable. Strengths and weaknesses across, opportunities and threats down, and each cell names the strategy the pairing implies: SO — achieve opportunities that greatly match the strengths; WO — overcome weaknesses to attain opportunities; ST — use strengths to reduce vulnerability to threats; WT — prevent weaknesses, to avoid becoming more susceptible to threats. A SWOT that stops at four lists is the failure the source names as its central one. This step is what the process exists to reach. It produces CANDIDATE strategies, not a chosen one, and they are not ranked — see the process documentation on why no scoring activity exists. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_Cross . Cut over candidate, extracted Retire the parent's copy and measure the cutover until it is complete or cannot be shown complete. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Call_Cutover . Cut over candidate, extracted Freeze the in-repo copy in the kept trashcan and measure the cutover until it is complete or cannot be shown complete. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Call_Cutover . Cut the subgraph that leaves candidate, extracted Apply the editorial scope mechanically and report what it removed. A selection that reports nothing cannot be told from one that ran over an empty rule. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#A_Select . Cutover: retire the parent's copy candidate, extracted The one commit worth reverting, made only after the parent consumes the release and every identifier dereferences. It retires the parent's copy, frozen, never refreshed and never rendered, rather than deleting it. Where the copy goes is the sub-kg-lifecycle skill's stage 13; this diagram does not name that store, because the published graph must not. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-cutover.bpmn#Task_Cutover .

a314da9b0f07.title: D
a314da9b0f07.content: Data model Entities + cardinalities candidate, extracted Between requirements and sign-off, and the order is the argument: requirements are statements about things, and the model says what the things ARE. Drafted earlier it is invented from nothing, since the entities come from the phase-2 BPA; drafted later, sign-off approves requirements whose nouns were never pinned — which is how two stakeholders approve one sentence meaning different things. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_DataModel . Decide each adaptation: keep, revise or retire candidate, extracted One recorded decision per affected adaptation, with its reason: keep it as is, revise it to the new version, or retire it because the new version now covers it. A decision to diverge from the new version is recorded as such. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/guideline-updates.bpmn#Task_Decide . Decide each theme candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/stalled-agent-triage.bpmn#U_Decide . Decide what may leave the repository candidate, extracted EDITORIAL, and it is stage 1 rather than a filter bolted to the exporter. kg-export produces the WHOLE graph because inspection wants the whole graph; a portal wants what its readers may see. Running the second as the first is how a QA verdict, a bean's blocking note or an unpublished draft reaches a public cache. Decided once, here, rather than at each consumer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#E_Scope . Decide, weighing the recommendations candidate, extracted public-comment decide, or decide: code on GitHub from a login in config.json editors. accepted, accepted-modified, not-accepted, noted, deferred; a reason for all but accepted. Also reopens a decided comment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Declare it in place, with its seam candidate, extracted <name>/<name>.json with name, version, repository (the planned home), livesAt (where it sits today), needs, and only the directories that exist, each declared with its files in one commit. <name>/platform.ts from the first commit, so no climb out of the directory ever needs rerouting. Scaffolded by init-folio --staged <path>, which writes those two files and nothing at the host root; never --instance, which writes a whole repository. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Declare . Declare the model where a tool can read it candidate, extracted A model in prose is a proposal; a model in the declaration is a model. Ship a reader in the same change: a model that is only documentation goes inert. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#A_Declare . Declare the mount: harness, repository, pin candidate, extracted A layer { name, source: { remote: { repository, ref } } } in the downstream's root index.config.json, written through writeDeclaredMounts. A folio with no index still reads remoteMounts on its declaration; both at once is refused. ref is a full 40-character commit. Overrides, if any, are keyed by layer name and then by directory id — never by path. The index itself is the index-config skill's. Decide first whether you want a remote mount at all: reading another graph without holding its code is a SUBSCRIPTION, not a mount. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_DeclareMount . Declare the node materialized candidate, extracted The node's state moves from referenced to materialized, carrying purpose, localPath, gates and (archival) fixity. There is NO default state: a node that has not said is invalid, because 'the author did not say' and 'the author said they could not tell' are different facts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Declare . Declare the purpose: working or archival candidate, extracted working or archival, and it is asked FIRST because three of the five gates mean different things under each. An archival copy keeps the original bytes, never expires, requires fixity, and is the only thing that discharges sourceLoss; a working copy keeps derived content and discharges none of that. A process that gated first and asked afterwards would be judging a copy whose obligations it did not yet know. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Purpose . Declare the web-app directory candidate, extracted The layer declares a directory of kind web-app in its <name>.json and puts a web-app.json (web-app/0.1.0) at its root: id, title, description, how it builds, the languages it ships (the site's six UN languages: ar, en, es, fr, ru, zh), the layer directories it reads at build time (contentFrom), a size budget, and for a copied app its licence and source. Its UI strings are one flat catalog in the source language (i18n.catalog). No publish script, no site.build.keep, no harness of its own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/web-app-publish.bpmn#A_Declare . Declare, detangle, isolate candidate, extracted The graph-detanglement practice, all of its gates: declared in place, zero wrong-direction edges on every axis, and standing alone with its own declaration, namespace and artefact. A plain task on purpose, not a call to graph-detanglement.bpmn: that process ends in its own authorise-and-extract steps, which here are stages 9-13 of this one, and calling it would run them twice. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Detangle . Deduplicate, and keep what is actually relevant candidate, extracted The paper's Refiner. Accumulates into the evidence set the report is built from — so what is dropped here is invisible downstream, which is why it is a step somebody performs rather than a filter buried in retrieval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn#A_Refine . Defer build and queue verify sweep candidate, extracted Set the preview/agent-build commit status on the PR head to pending, post the preview-build-verify notice on the PR, and exit the critical-path run so the runner is free. Off the critical path, preview-verify-sweep.yml (on staging workflow completion and every 15 minutes) waits until no Feature Staging run is active or queued, selects the oldest open PR whose head still has preview/agent-build = pending, and dispatches feature-staging.yml with verify_pr to rebuild and verify the agent's preview. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_Defer . Deploy the MVP to staging candidate, extracted An MVP is shared AS A branches/ DEPLOY, not as a description of one. feature-staging.yml publishes the branch under branches/<branch-slug>/ on gh-pages and comments the URL on the PR, so the stakeholder who tests it is looking at the built artefact rather than at a screenshot — the same argument the merge discipline makes about rendered work: holding a rendered change back for assessment makes assessment harder, not safer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_DeployStaging . Deploy the preview site candidate, extracted A preview never seeds the shared cache. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_DeployPreview . Deploy the rendering candidate, extracted publish-site.ts commits the staged tree onto gh-pages as a full replace (run by the instance's Pages workflow on a push to main, or by an agent with its own git credentials); GitHub Pages then builds it from the branch. Rebuild and retry on a rejected push; never rebase the branch. The report names the gh-pages commit SHA. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Deploy . Deploy the site candidate, extracted Deploy the site built from main or a release. Deploying is release-management, after a human authorised the release — an agent never records that authorisation. A release's files are not deployed to the site: a v* tag makes a GitHub draft release carrying them (ig-release.yml; skill ig-binary-artefacts §"Releasing"), which the owner publishes. Report the published URL only once it answers: a returned deploy is not a serving site. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_Deploy . Deploy to branches/<slug>/ candidate, extracted The stage job copies the built site into gh-pages under branches/<branch-slug>/, then staging-share.ts apply keeps only the files that differ from the live site. The preview's staging-sw.js serves every other file from the live site and puts the staging banner back on it. Other previews and the main site are left as they are. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-stage.bpmn#Task_DeployStaging . Derive content from the assets candidate, extracted See ingest-derive-content.bpmn. Most of this subprocess is not implemented yet. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Derive . Derive the key candidate, extracted qa:publish --github reads the event: a push to main publishes under main/<sha>/, a pull request under pr/<n>/<head-sha>/ — the head that was tested, not the merge ref. It also reads whether the token can write, which the gateway after it routes on. The key is main/<sha> or pr/<n>/<sha>. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/qa-publish.bpmn#Task_DeriveKey . Derive the metamodel in use candidate, extracted Tool archimate-metamodel (archimate:metamodel --check, on the layer root): the element types the model uses and every (source type, relationship, target type) pattern, each checked against ArchiMate's relationship table. Placeholder elements named after their own type are reported, never fatal: removing them is the author's call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/archimate-publish.bpmn#A_Metamodel . Derive the slug from the head ref candidate, extracted Derive the slug from the PR's head ref: every character outside [a-zA-Z0-9._-] becomes '-', runs of '-' collapse, and leading or trailing '-' is trimmed. It must be one safe path segment, checked by value. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/feature-staging.bpmn#Task_Slug . Describe the desired change candidate, extracted Author describes the content change in natural language. Example: "Update the immunization schedule to add a booster at 18 months." . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review.bpmn#Task_DescribeChange . Describe the intended change candidate, extracted The editor states the change in natural language; no content has moved yet. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_DescribeChange . Describe the need (chat, issue, discussion) candidate, extracted The BA describes the capability gap in their own words. They do not need to know it is called CRDM. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#BA_Submit . Design review candidate, extracted cat-harness Process_WireframeDesignReview: as-is use for a form that exists, design use for one being designed. This process does not restate the method. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/questionnaire-wireframe-review.bpmn#Call_Review . Detect change scope & impact candidate, extracted Agent analyses the requested change: - Which content blocks are affected? - Are there downstream implications (indicators, referral logic, visit schedules)? - Will deterministic logic (CQL/DMN) need updating? skill: content-graph, integration-watcher . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_DetectScope . Detect feature request (crdm-detect skill) candidate, extracted Recognise the request as a platform capability change rather than content work, from crdm-detect's signals. Never call it "CRDM" to the person. Mid-content-work, ask whether to pause for requirements now or record a work item for later — do not switch on your own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#A_Detect . Detect media type, mint a doc id candidate, extracted Sniff the media type rather than trusting the extension, and mint the doc id from the page-1 arXiv stamp where there is one, else from the filename. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Detect . Detect the interaction modality candidate, extracted Before the first question is asked, establish HOW to ask it: audio, ordinary chat, selectable options for a user with limited hand function, large-type for low vision. A user who finds the questions unusable never reaches the rest of this diagram. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_DetectModality . Detect what moved candidate, extracted translation:status --instance <root> for new, obsolete and fuzzy strings, and the instance's template check. Either failing, or showing anything but zero, is a change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Detect . Determine the content type and its specialisation candidate, extracted Read the folio's contentType and the specialisation registered for it (TestDataSpecialisationSchema in schemas/sdlc/test-data.ts): fhir-templating for FHIR IG and DAK content, markdown-fixture for document folios, lean-counterexample for proof folios, tabular-cohort for aggregate indicator tables. None registered stops here and says so, rather than guessing one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/test-data-curation.bpmn#Task_DetermineSpecialisation . Determine the context: what is known, and already decided candidate, extracted Before composing anything: what is already known, each fact with where it came from; which declaration governs the matter (the layer's <name>.json, the diagram the caller is in, the Skill its task names); what state is recorded; and whether the question has ALREADY been decided — by the person earlier in the conversation, or in a declaration that quotes their ruling. A settled question is not asked again: asking it reopens a decision and spends the person's attention twice. Read it, do not remember it: cite what you read. What the caller handed in is checked here, not re-derived. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineContext . Determine the process and task, or that you are idle candidate, extracted Name the Process, the lane and the task the question belongs to, and say so in the message: "Process: Initialize a harness, at Determine the harness and repositories, as the Bootstrapping Agent". A reader who does not know which process you are in will assume the last one's rules still hold. If you are in no Process, that is an answer too: you are IDLE, and what you are doing is classifying a request to find the Process it belongs to — say that, rather than presenting a question as though a step had asked for it. You are OUT of process, and it is undetermined, when you cannot name the Process, when two candidates fit, when the step you believed was next is not the one the diagram enables, or when the work in hand was not what you said you would do. Do not infer your way back in. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineProcess . Determine the roles: which you act as, and the person's candidate, extracted An Actor performs a task in a Process AS a Role. Nothing is a Role by nature: the same agent is the Bootstrapping Agent in one diagram and another Role in the next, and which one it is depends on the lane of the task it is performing now. So say which Role you are acting as — the lane of the CALLING task, since this lane is variable — and which Role the person you ask holds (the Requestor, or whoever the calling lane names). It decides what you may ask them for: only the Requestor chooses a harness, and a question put to somebody who does not hold the decision gets an answer that settles nothing. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineRoles . Determine where you are: process, roles, context candidate, extracted Before narrowing, say where this is happening, in the words you will use in the question. PROCESS: Initialize a harness, at its first step, inside Determine the harness and repositories — the only place a Bootstrapping Agent can be (FR-2). If you cannot say that (you were started some other way, or a step you believed done is not), you are out of process: do not infer your way back in. ROLES: you act as the Bootstrapping Agent because you were told so; the person you will ask is the Requestor — the one who asked for the harness, and the only one who may choose it. A request relayed by somebody else leaves the Requestor undetermined. CONTEXT: what the request said, and what the checkout holds — a declaration at its root, a harness named in the request. Whatever cannot be determined is handed to the called discussion as undetermined, and asked about first; it is never filled with a default. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineWhere . Determine which CDN, the root URL and the Subgraphs candidate, extracted Every Subgraph id asked for must be one the declaration lists; none means the whole graph. The root URL is the one given. The target's Tool is the one that satisfies: ["render-kg-to-cdn"] for that CDN — gh-pages for GitHub Pages. A caller that already rendered and verified its tree hands the tree over instead of the graph, and the Tool pushes it without rendering again. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/render-kg-to-cdn.bpmn#Task_Resolve . Determine which harness, and where candidate, extracted The candidates are listed and the Requestor is asked, in discussion, which asks through human-agent-discussion. IN: nothing but the context this agent was handed. OUT: zero or ONE harness, and the locations — a document conforming to discussion.output.schema.json. One at most: a list of two is not an answer, and the Bootstrapping Agent may not break the tie itself. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_DetermineHarness . Diff the two ASTs candidate, extracted ig-ast.ts diff <base> <head> --plan plan.json --site <site>/ast-delta/: resources added, removed, changed (with an element-level differential) and version-changed; edges added and removed; the plan's decision. Every page opens with the provisional mark and is wrapped in raw so narrative Liquid is not executed. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-ast-delta-review.bpmn#Task_Diff . Discard all entries, or a whole session candidate, extracted Remove every entry, one session's, or those before a date — emptyLog with { all }, { session } or { before }; there is no default selector. A file that will not parse is kept, and the result must say what was refused and why, not only what was removed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_EmptyAll . Discard one entry by id candidate, extracted Remove one entry by its stable id, with emptyLog({ id }). Logs are the one exception to the never-delete rule because an entry records no decision; the exception covers files that declare folio-log/v1, not the directory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_EmptyOne . Discuss it with the person candidate, extracted Bootstrap's human-agent discussion, given the composed question. Its Ask ONE question step is where this harness's delivery rule applies: Post the whole composed question as ordinary chat text BEFORE any card. This is the copy that survives: a card, once answered, shows only the chosen option, and a dismissed card shows nothing. Never "see the card", never a request for a typed reply such as "1y 2n". Then the card: Whatever the host calls its selection tool (AskUserQuestion, request_decision, a button card): the same letters and labels as the chat text, the recommended option marked. No host card tool: say so in the chat and keep each answer to one short choice. Its answer step: One tap on the card, or any answer the person prefers to give. Free text is always available and never required. A dismissal is NOT an answer and never selects the default as a choice; the question stays open in the chat. On an answer: Hand the answer back to the calling step, quoted. If it settles how a kind of thing is decided, it is a rule: write it into the governing skill in the same turn. On no answer: Do what the question said would happen with no answer, and say so. Nothing irreversible proceeds on a default: such a step waits for the person. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/ask-the-person.bpmn#Call_Discuss . Dispatch a fixer candidate, extracted One fixer agent per cause, never one per repository. Give it the failing run, the cause and the repository: pins out of step go to the next re-pin train on the index; the layer's own bug to a fix PR in that layer; a lower layer's bug to a fix PR in the lower layer, then a re-pin. It opens a draft fix PR, linked from the main-red issue. The fix is a non-content P0 PR and follows the normal merge rules: the six-line request, the owner's batch card, full-tier CI green as judged. Close the loop when the next main run is green and the main-red issue closes. Never silence the failure, and never skip, disable or quarantine a gate or a test. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-manager-watch.bpmn#Task_DispatchFixer . Dispatch AST refresh candidate, extracted Actions → "IG AST refresh (by hand)" → Run workflow on the default branch, inputs ref = the default branch, force = false. Set force = true only to rebuild a cache that is valid but suspected wrong. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/content/ig-ast-cache.bpmn#Task_Dispatch . Dispatch one agent, recorded on the bean candidate, extracted Before the agent starts: the date, why the fail condition fired, the agent's id, its budget. Never while the first writer may still be live. Two failed attempts with the same cause go to the owner instead. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_Dispatch . Dispatch with adjudicator_sees — never the artefact candidate, extracted UntaintedDispatch on the criterion declares what each party is given; the caller names a subject and a criterion and does not hand-assemble a brief, because the party composing a brief by hand is the producer. untaintedPartitionDefects reports overlap when the checker and the adjudicator can read the same file — one of them is then grading its own input, and the verdict measures nothing while raising no error. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/adjudication.bpmn#A_Dispatch . Distribute to the public candidate, extracted The committee and the editor send the announcement through their channels. Comment is open from here until the agreed close. Skill: public-comment. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment-release.bpmn#Task_Distribute . Do it, then check again candidate, extracted Only what the agent, or a tool it has, can do without replacing anything somebody wrote: regenerate a README section, add a missing Pages workflow, switch Pages on with an authenticated gh. Performing is not the same as done: the flow goes back to the check, and only the check says done. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_PerformStep . Do the work candidate, extracted The task itself. This diagram says nothing about how it is done; it only brackets it, so that a reader of the log can tell where one run of work began and ended. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/activity-log.bpmn#A_DoWork . Draft the block edit candidate, extracted The authoring agent produces a PROPOSED change. Nothing is written to the corpus yet. For a rendered change it also produces the before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) here, before Gateway_ValidationFork, so the preview exists when the parallel review starts. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_DraftEdit . Draft, review and publish candidate, extracted See draft-to-publication.bpmn. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#CallActivity_Publication . Drain: land, close or re-target the open PRs candidate, extracted Work the PRs seed:ready named until the source settles: land or close the heavy movers and the next layer's PRs, bring the layer's open PRs to five or fewer, and finish any move in flight. Fix a red rehearsal or a discovery miss where it is. Nothing is seeded from here; it goes back to the gateway, which re-asks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_Drain . Drain: land, close or re-target the open PRs candidate, extracted Work the PRs seed:ready named until the source settles: land or close the heavy movers and the next layer's PRs, bring the layer's open PRs to five or fewer, and finish any move in flight. Fix a red rehearsal or a discovery miss where it is. Nothing is seeded from here; it goes back to the gateway, which re-asks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-move.bpmn#Task_Drain . Draw the board of todos and beans candidate, extracted The todo board mounts inside the landing board, so harness cards and todo stickies share one surface. Each card carries an edit link only when the build composed one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Board . Draw the sample candidate, extracted On a first translation: every diagram label, every persona and scenario string, and a seeded random fraction of the rest, with the seed written down so the sample can be drawn again. On a refresh: only the strings that were new or fuzzy. Hand the back-translator the msgstr values alone, keyed by an opaque id. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-round-trip.bpmn#Task_RT_Sample . Drop its positions and sweep orphans candidate, extracted Only after the content has moved: drop its positions from the layout layer and sweep any position whose note is now gone. Sweeping first would make the board authoritative over the folio for one step. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_UpdateLayer . Drop the file in the queue candidate, extracted Through the forge's upload form, a commit, or any other route that lands the file in the declared queue. The agent watches rather than chases: an arrival may be minutes or days away. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#P_Upload . Dry-run, then ask the owner naming every PR candidate, extracted Stack the PRs on a meta-merge branch without pushing. Then post the full question (include, leave out with the reason, merge method, per repository), followed by the card: A go, B also the red ones, C dry run only, D cancel. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/saturation-meta-merge.bpmn#Task_Ask .

2c9002f96ae3.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, E–Q
2c9002f96ae3.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 639 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 229 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 308 terms and is 265 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 956 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 308 shown . E F G H I J K L M N O P Q

c454425edb02.title: E
c454425edb02.content: Edit deterministic logic (if needed) candidate, extracted If the content change affects decision logic, indicators, or workflows: - Update CQL expressions - Update DMN decision tables - Adjust indicator definitions skill: dak-authoring, fhir-pipeline . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_EditLogic . Edit it in place — it is your own content candidate, extracted The ordinary path, drawn so the process does not read as though every edit needs a copy. Content in a writable directory is authored content and is edited where it lives; the copy-out is for somebody else's bytes, not for yours. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/copy-out-materialized.bpmn#Task_EditDirectly . Edit narrative content blocks candidate, extracted Agent modifies the relevant content blocks (.md files, block manifests). Validates each edit against the schema (content_validate). skill: content editing, block builders . BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Task_EditContent . Edit the document as decided, on a feature branch candidate, extracted public-comment edit --branch: the author (human, or an agent in the author role) edits the folio's blocks as the decision says, on a feature branch for one change-set. Its PR says Closes #N for the change-set issue, and opening it moves that issue's accepted comments to editing. Before its preview is staged, the author writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per comment (No. 136: Accepted...), starting from each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, after an optional Overall statement. Quality check: every comment number in the change set has a disposition; the sheet flags gaps and words that differ from the people's. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_AuthorEdits . Edit the document in the row's pull request candidate, extracted One row, one branch, one active pull request: the agent edits on the row's branch and opens its pull request, or updates it when the row comes round again. A closed pull request the committee wants back is reopened, or replaced by a new one on the same branch; earlier ones stay listed in Agentic status. Agentic status (Green) says where it is, and Staging review opens the preview's what-changed page. Before the preview is staged, the agent writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per feedback item, starting from the people's Blue Disposition, after an optional Overall statement; the sheet shows it in Disposition (agent) and flags any item without a disposition, or one that differs from the people's. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_EditInPullRequest . Edit the flagged passage and re-inject candidate, extracted The reviewer corrects the passage in the PO rather than sending the whole translation back. Flows to Task_PoInject, so the round-trip QA runs again over the corrected text — "edit the translation and re-run QA", which is what the adjudication step has always offered and what this process could not do. A userTask, not a service task: this is the one step here where a person edits content, and the lane's actor is the reviewer who just adjudicated. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_EditTranslation . Edit, comment or raise todos on the folio's copy candidate, extracted The copied asset is now writable content of the target folio with recorded upstream provenance (KgAsset.source). The folio author may edit it in place, attach review comments, or raise todos (todo-manager) against it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/copy-into-folio.bpmn#Task_WorkOnCopy . Editing and HCI validation candidate, extracted See editing-hci-validation.bpmn. Runs once per proposed change, not once per cycle. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#CallActivity_Editing . Editing and HCI validation candidate, extracted The editing sub-process. Every change to the corpus goes through its HCI validation gate — a red draft is fixed there, never by patching the built artifact. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#CallActivity_Editing . Eject the culprit, record why candidate, extracted T1 (R3; SQ19 §2.2 p. 3): the culprit leaves, the rest re-run. Writes ejection on its queue entry (train id, reason, evidence URL, when) and a dated evidence snapshot on this instance. The train is never rejected whole for one member. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Task_Eject . Elect the merge manager with the siblings candidate, extracted The deterministic rule (electHolder): the active session that owns the P0 PR, else the earliest-created active session, the session id breaking a tie. Stalled sessions are not candidates. Every sibling computes the same answer from the same listing (owner ruling, 2026-11-07). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-request.bpmn#Sib_Elect . End-to-end + accessibility (HARD) candidate, extracted Install Chromium, check the rendered BPMN SVGs are current, then run the Playwright suite, which includes the accessibility checks. Hard: a failure blocks the PR. SHARDED since bean dlqu (drawn as one task, deliberately: a multi-instance marker would add a BPMN term to every instance's UML overview, about 75 generated files, for a picture this sentence already gives): the suite runs as three e2e-shard jobs (E2E_SHARD=i/3, one Playwright worker per core in each), and each shard is its own required check, so a shard that failed, was cancelled or never ran is a red check of its own. Until bean 5p4m (issue #2456) an e2e job carried one check name for the three and completed the task only when every instance succeeded; it was ~1 s of work behind a runner request that waited minutes, and was removed. Measured before the split: playwright test alone was 4m33s of a 5m16s job, the workflow's slowest once bun test ran in parallel. The BPMN-render and .bat-wrapper checks run in shard 1 only, so they are asked once. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/code-quality-gates.bpmn#Task_E2E . Ensure the publication-manager label candidate, extracted The alert is a tracking issue labelled publication-manager — the role, not a person, because no actor declares a GitHub account for it. Whoever watches that label is alerted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/publish-alert.bpmn#A_Label . Ensure the tracking label exists candidate, extracted Create the tracking label (the label input) with --force so it exists before either issue path runs — the close path filters on it too, and on a repository that has never had a finding it would not exist yet. Skipped on an unknown verdict. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_EnsureTrackingLabel . Ensure the tracking label exists candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/tracked-watch.bpmn#Task_Label . Enumerate the source descriptor candidate, extracted Resolve the request against the source's descriptor (one per corpus, in the declared sources/ of the layer that owns it, e.g. who-iris/sources/), read against cat-harness/schemas/library/source-descriptor.ts BEFORE any gate. Three things come from it and none may be guessed. (1) Which subset strategies the source supports — supportsSubset(). (2) Whether a subset stands on its own: when subsetIsSelfContained is false (mathlib), the request is closed over its dependencies here, and every gate after this one is asked about the CLOSURE, because a subset that omits what its members depend on is not a smaller corpus, it is one that does not build. (3) What enumerating the whole costs — enumerationCost(), which is undefined when the descriptor has no measured denominator; SIZE then refuses rather than estimates. A source with no descriptor is not an error here: it is an unknown, and SIZE refuses on it. The descriptor is CALLED here rather than restated. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Enumerate . Establish origin and licence candidate, extracted Authors, publication, identifier, and the licence the source itself states. No stated licence means reference only: headings, page ranges and a summary in our own words; the file stays in uploads/ (git-ignored) pinned by checksum. A method with no origin is a house process; write a skill instead. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/methodology-from-source.bpmn#A_Origin . Establish the licence from the upload candidate, extracted EARLY: before any derivation, because library/ is holds: content and anything derived first is committed, so refusing it later is a deletion nobody may take unasked. This step sees only the upload itself — the licence recorded in its intake.json (the same stated / unknown record a library manifest carries) and whether a LICENSE file sits beside it. It never infers a licence from extracted text. The verdict is stated, unknown, or UNDETERMINED, and undetermined is never reported as cleared: the pipeline proceeds and says so, because a licence that only extraction can reveal is a later check's to find. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_Licence . Establish who is acting candidate, extracted The first step and not a formality: actor is the one field of the record that nothing else can supply. Every other field is recoverable by reading the repository; who is acting is not. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_IdentifyActor . Every identifier dereferences candidate, extracted After the release is live, every published identifier resolves to the file it names. Where cat-harness.sdlc is switched on, this step is the opt-in process publish-verification (Process_PublishVerification, sdlc/processes/publish-verification.bpmn); it is not called from here, because a layer without that sub-graph does not have it (owner card Q-OPTIN-CALLS A, 2026-11-12). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-move.bpmn#Task_Verify . Every skill and tool used becomes a Tool candidate, extracted Each script, CLI or checker the process relies on gets a Tool node (tools/<id>/<id>.json) that satisfies a named skill, validated by folio-assistant's ToolDefinitionSchema. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/methodology-from-source.bpmn#A_Tools . Execute every case, or skip it with a reason candidate, extracted Every case in dependency order. A case is executed or explicitly skipped with its reason; a case that simply has no verdict is a finding, because it cannot be told from a case nobody ran. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/test-plan-execution.bpmn#A_Execute . Explain each missing permission, with the exact config diff candidate, extracted Per permission: what it allows the agent to do without asking, why a process here needs it, the narrowest form that would do, and the exact change to the Tool's config. Context, options, recommendation, question (interaction-modality §4.1). Least privilege is the recommendation unless there is a measured reason for more. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/secure-agent-permissions.bpmn#Task_Explain . Export the knowledge graph and its schema candidate, extracted Exports the knowledge graph and its schema into the published tree (kg-export.ts, harness-schema-export.ts, kg-viewer.ts), stripping the unpublished graph typologies, then runs the built-site checks: every maintained artefact is present (bun run cat check:maintained-artefacts), no block-level markup escaped (check:escaped-markup), the QA witnesses and results are published, and the navbar tiles resolve. Each outcome is recorded, not acted on: Task_Judge judges them after the push. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/docs-site-publish.bpmn#Task_Export . Extract claim candidates candidate, extracted candidates.json holds extracted theorems and definitions. Proposals only -- never adjudicated verdicts. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-extract-structure.bpmn#Task_Candidates . Extract every template once candidate, extracted Once, for every locale: the .pot templates for the pages, the diagrams (translate-bpmn --extract) and the glossary schemes, each by the layer's own extractor. A locale that would need a different template is a defect in the extraction, not a reason to extract again. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_Extract . Extract figures and tables candidate, extracted The pdf-images.py, pdf-vector-labels.py and pdf-vector-figures.py arms extract the raster images and the figures drawn as vectors (grouped and rendered). For every table the document's structure declares, an agent reads the rendered page, checks cell text against the text layer, and writes tables/<label>.csv plus tables.csvw.json (folio-tabular-csvw/v1), with a draft description in the six UN languages; pdf-tables.py's grid is a cross-check, not the answer. Owner, 2026-11-11 (who-iris): "actually extract the figures" and "any tables too". Method: skill document-intake, "Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe". BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_FiguresTables . Extract its metadata into the KG candidate, extracted THE METADATA STEP. What enters the knowledge graph is the asset's INDEX — what it is, how big, what type, when it says it was written — and, for a container, what is in it; its contents do not go in unless somebody asks, with a reason. The tool is cat-harness-tools/scripts/extract-assets.ts, writing a folio-extraction/v1 record (schemas/content/extraction.ts). The media type is sniffed from the leading bytes, never taken from the extension. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/document-ingestion.bpmn#Task_ExtractMetadata . Extract reference lists candidate, extracted Each reference list of the source (a References, Bibliography or Further reading section, in any of the six UN languages) becomes folio-reference/v1 nodes with the Tool references-extract: one node per cited work, provenance extracted, derivedFrom the section it was read from, and printed the entry exactly as the source prints it. Only fields read without guessing are set (address, DOI, ISBN, year, access date); a cited IRIS item the library holds gets heldAt. The nodes are the document's own bibliography on the bibliography page. A source with no reference list skips this step with nothing written. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn#Task_References . Extract structure candidate, extracted See ingest-extract-structure.bpmn. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/library/l1-document-ingestion.bpmn#CallActivity_Extract . Extract the app's translation templates candidate, extracted Tool web-app-build (web-apps:build --extract): the catalog becomes translations/<locale>/apps/<id>.pot in the declaring layer, one ui-string entry per key with the key as msgctxt. This is the app's "refresh the templates" step, named in the layer's AGENTS.md so the translation watcher runs it too. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/web-app-publish.bpmn#A_Extract . Extract the POT candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_ExtractPOT . Extract the text layer candidate, extracted The document has a text layer: extract it with pdf-extract (pdfminer.six, then a zero-dependency content-stream reader). Exit 2 means no text layer — a scan — and routes to OCR; it is not an empty document. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-extract-structure.bpmn#Task_ExtractText . Extract translatable strings (POT) candidate, extracted Scan the source content and write the translatable strings to .pot files at the configured granularity: segment prose by paragraph, shield what must not be translated (math, code, labels, Lean companions) as placeholders, normalise whitespace, and extract metadata such as titles, alt text and captions. Tool: the translation_extract MCP tool. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_ExtractPot . Extract translatable strings (POT) candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_PotExtract .

4f6b562786b3.title: F
4f6b562786b3.content: Feature sign-off on issue candidate, extracted Stakeholders sign off on the delivered feature on the issue, having tested the built artefact rather than a description of it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#S_FeatureSignoff . Fetch and validate the pinned declaration candidate, extracted A sparse, shallow fetch of the substrate's root declaration only. Two questions: does it parse as bootstrap's KnowledgeGraphDeclarationSchema, and does it declare at least one harness? could not fetch is a third answer and is never read as conforms. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Validate . Fetch, and record fixity candidate, extracted Fetch, then record sha256 and byte count. Fixity is REQUIRED for an archival copy: an archive that cannot demonstrate it is unchanged is a copy, and it cannot be re-fetched to check, because the thing it would be re-fetched from is what it exists to survive. The data already exists — every structure.json carries sha256 and bytes, and nothing reads them as fixity. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Fetch . FHIR IG ASTs: Process_IgAstCache candidate, extracted Component 4b, in its own lane: the FHIR IG layer's IG AST cache, Process_IgAstCache (declared by that layer), integrated, not replaced. It is drawn as a task because this layer may not name a process of a layer above it; the steps are that process's. RESTORE: read the cached AST from its branch store and judge it — that process's "valid for this commit?" IS this component's verify (class a: the AST is judged against this commit's IG sources and tooling); valid → the site is built from it. SAVE: that process's own path, not cached-step — a miss dispatches an AST refresh on a Java runner with 10 GB, which rewrites the branch store. The branch store is a cache node (fhir-ast, fhir-harness caches/fhir-ast.cache.json). Owner: CI speed 12, the IG layers' session. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_IgAst . File feedback as beans candidate, extracted Triaged feedback re-enters the work plan as beans, which is how the next cycle knows what it is for. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_FeedbackBeans . File info, sizes, hashes, timestamps, mimetype candidate, extracted NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Mechanical and cheap; the checksum is what makes a remote asset verifiable. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_TechMeta . File QC findings as beans candidate, extracted QC failed on the aggregate: file each finding as a bean, so it is tracked on the work plan rather than lost in qa.json. Check for an existing bean before creating one. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/ig-incremental-build.bpmn#Task_QcBeans . File QC findings as beans candidate, extracted Each QC finding becomes a bean on the work plan, which the modeller and the agents both see. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn#Task_QcBeans . File the adjudication issue candidate, extracted Submit opens GitHub's new-issue form prefilled with a readable summary and a translation-adjudication/v1 JSON block, labelled translation-adjudication and titled [translation review] …. When the record is too long for a URL the page copies the body for pasting instead. Filing it is the act of adjudicating. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-review-adjudication.bpmn#Task_TRA_FileIssue . File the signed certification candidate, extracted The signed certification goes under the declared attestations graph on main (owner ruling D2 (a), D5 default), pointing at the report it certifies. The bean resolves here, once the process has actually finished. Files it as qa-attestations/v1. Filter the corpus, choose the granularity, decompose the question candidate, extracted The paper's Planner. Three outputs, and the middle one is the method's substance: a filtered document subset, the granularity to search at, and the sub-questions. CHOOSING THE GRANULARITY PER QUESTION is the whole point of parsing at several. A broad question is answered from summaries and a specific one from chunks; a pipeline that picks once has answered every future question the same way. This checkout cannot yet offer the choice — l1-blocks.ts produces blocks, there is no summary level — so this step SAYS which granularity it searched rather than implying the corpus offered alternatives. Re-entered on every iteration, not only the first: the sub-questions are re-derived from what has been found so far, which is what makes the loop a search rather than a retry. 9754287295af.title: G
9754287295af.content: Gate every slice: slice:sqlite:check candidate, extracted For every slice: build twice and require one sha256; read the row digest back from the file and require it to equal the digest computed from the source without SQLite; run an FTS5 phrase query for a known row; and audit the payloads with auditPayloadTree (deploy payloads as written, the kg slice's pointers against the committed payload tree). A slice whose rows do not match its source fails; it never passes as whole. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Check . Gate results: restore / save candidate, extracted Component 2c. RESTORE: the result store (build/result-store/) and the CI cone records, by prefix — a WARM start: the cone (ci-cone.ts) then matches each stored entry exactly (fingerprint from cache:key --base, every recorded path state, every replayed git answer) and only an exact match is reported SKIPPED, never passed. A committer's local gate record is class (b): honoured on the critical path, then re-verified off it. SAVE: main only (class c for CI's records). Owner roles: the gate-reuse session (CI speed 8) and the committer-side session (CI speed 3). cache nodes: result-store, ci-cone, local-gate-records. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/cache.bpmn#Task_Gates . Gather and verify the evidence candidate, extracted Before anything is drafted: the author reads the guidance ALREADY in this content, frames the question as PICO, retrieves candidates across the three evidence classes, and has each candidate's authority resolved against its publisher's own API. A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none, and a figure redrawn from its own source adds none -- and the subprocess's first gateway (Gateway_RecommendationInPlay) ends it there at its own event, recording the answer, rather than satisfying the search vacuously. Writes <instance>/docs/ from the artefact index: one thin page per artefact with its JSON-LD node, and, for an instance whose docs declare igSite, only a front-matter artifacts.md. Built at publish, never committed. BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/processes/tools/ig-docs-site-compose.bpmn#Task_Pages . Generated sets: QA copy, pages candidate, extracted Component 2d. RESTORE: the QA working copy and the publish-time pages, keyed by bundle-cache.sh digest (the tree and the exact tool versions). A bundle is checked against the manifest it carries AND a source rule (the source run's head is this head, a parent, or a commit with this tree; or a main-scoped save) — class (a′), because a manifest alone proves a bundle intact, not built from these inputs. Hits across commits wait on the producers being byte-reproducible (the determinism audit). SAVE: the run that built it, recorded; main's records are read by every branch. Owner role: the generated-sets session (CI speed 10); the preview's copy, the preview session (CI speed 2). cache nodes: qa-working-copy, publish-pages. It reports one line in cached-step's format — cached-step <step>: hit|warm|miss (<trust>) — <why>. Key <key>. — to the job summary, which the daily hit-rate report counts. Grant a dispensation, with its reason candidate, extracted The rule applies and this subject is a stated exception. A kind: "human" entry with result: "pass" overrides the script's fail for that criterion, and ONLY while its field_hash matches the current source — so the dispensation is scoped to the version it was granted against, lapses when the block changes, and never becomes precedent. There is nothing to overturn later; the source moving overturns it. A dispensation with no notes is not a dispensation. It is an override somebody applied to get to green, and nobody can review it afterwards — which is why this step is not relaxable. 2ac86f02838a.content: Hand back to the discussion candidate, extracted The composed question goes, unchanged, to the discussion agent, which asks it through this same process on its yes branch and routes the answer back: the sibling's half of Process_HandBackToDiscussion (a task here, not a call, because that process calls this one). The sibling also shows it in its own thread, never only there. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/ask-the-person.bpmn#A_HandBack . The fail condition: no started line within 4 h, no push within 24 h, the session gone, or blocked on something it cannot settle. One line to the session; the instructions are in the bean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_HandBack . The merger does not fix the PR to make it pass. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn#Call_HandBack . R4: the PR returns with its reason. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/merge-train.bpmn#Call_HandBack . Then keep working on the recommended option where it can be undone, or stop if blocking. Hand new feedback to the row's agent; take over stalled rows candidate, extracted On every poll, changed or not, new Blue feedback goes verbatim to the agent working the row, and a stalled row is restarted or taken over. For each row: new Blue feedback goes, verbatim and in the same poll, to the thread that owns the row (named in its Agent row or Feedback (agent)), and Feedback (agent) says who has it. A row is stalled when its Blue cells changed, or Ready for agent turned Yes, more than 10 minutes ago and no Agent step was recorded since; or when its agent recorded no step for 2 hours. A stalled row's owning thread is asked once; with no answer within 10 minutes, or a thread that is done or stopped, the watcher takes the row over, or asks the coordinator for a new thread, and writes the new owner, the step and a link into Feedback (agent). SWOT does not make that selection and does not make the decision. What is handed over includes the ambiguities from A_RecordAmbiguous and the fact that the candidates are UNRANKED. A receiving methodology that assumed an ordered list would be reading a priority SWOT never established. It is not: merging approves the CHANGE, and this approves what a reader will actually see. A description cannot stand in for it (continual-progress). a7ee7ac7ae92.content: Identify content and target locale candidate, extracted The coordinator selects: - Which content nodes need translation (block, section, chapter, or folio) - The target locale (one of the supportedLocales in <name>.config.json) - The priority and deadline . BPMN activities of fhir-harness · source fhir-harness/collab/processes/content/l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn#Task_IgPublisher . Impact analysis what of ours binds it candidate, extracted The half a changelog cannot supply, because upstream does not know what you reached into. Worked from the row's binds list in upstream-pins.json. For the theme: site-chrome/assets/js/docs-ui.js MOVES the theme's own search markup into the action launcher and binds .search, #search-input and .search-label; docs-ui.css overrides .side-bar, .site-header and .main-header; three e2e specs assert the structure the theme emits. An upstream rename of any of those is not a build failure — it is a shipped feature that quietly stops working. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#A_Impact . Import hygiene (HARD) and advisories (WARN-ONLY) candidate, extracted FOUR QUESTIONS, ONE RUNNER — bean 7fu5. They were four jobs (lean-bare-import, python-imports, rust-wildcard, dependency-advisories), each about a second of work behind a ~13 s checkout and a runner request; measured on main run 37133247484 (2026-10-03), the run took 21.7 min while its longest job executed for 174 s, the rest waiting for runners. Now they are steps of the hygiene job, and every step after the first gate runs if: !cancelled(), so a red one masks none of the others — the om30 rule kept inside one job rather than by splitting it. (1) Lean, HARD: fail on any bare import Mathlib in content/**/*.lean; in this platform repo there is no content/, so the step prints SKIP and states that nothing was scanned. (2) Python, HARD: ruff F401 (unused) and F403 (wildcard) over the Python trees that exist, then the Python tests; an absent tree is dropped rather than passed to ruff, and an empty set says SKIP. (3) Dependency advisories, WARN-ONLY by the owner's ruling on bean j41m: is anything in the resolved tree KNOWN-VULNERABLE? The script exits 0 in every state and keeps them apart in its output; .github/dependabot.yml is the other half of that ruling and is not drawn here. (4) Rust wildcard imports, WARN-ONLY: report non-test use …::*; in tools/**/*.rs; continue-on-error, and therefore the job's LAST step, where it masks nothing. Until 2026-10-09 this was two steps here, Task_Release in the owner's lane bound to interaction-modality and Task_Land bound to prepare-merge; neither could refuse a merge, and neither said what happens when a repository has no CI. R1 still holds: what lands is exactly what CI tested. If main moved after the train's CI started, re-run rather than land. Each member's trainId is cleared, and its preview is then taken down by feature-staging.bpmn. A member the sub-process does not merge (held, refused, handed back) leaves the train with its reason on its queue entry. bd22b61a7110.content: OCR to ocr/page-*.txt candidate, extracted Each page is read in the document's languages (--lang-hint, from dc.language.iso), narrowed to the script the page shows. A page Tesseract is unsure of (mean word confidence under 70) is read again with each other installed script added, and the most confident read is kept: a French article's Arabic abstract, or the Latin URLs in an Arabic document's references. A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently ("Manual" and "Manval"), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. Options analysis accept · revise · discard candidate, extracted On the edge out of Task_ReviewFindings and before Task_RecordDecision: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after Task_RecordDecision the decision is already written down. In the Agent lane: the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED (its own decision-audit note), and Task_RecordDecision in Lane_Editor records WHAT WAS CHOSEN. The analyst is not the decider. (CallActivity_Evidence is in Lane_Editor because the author performs the retrieval.) Everything the decider needs exists by the time the reviewer has finished and the fixable findings are fixed. In the Agent lane, because this step produces the analysis and does not make the decision — PM_Decide is a userTask whose lane admits person only, and putting the analysis in the agent's lane is what keeps that separation legible rather than implied. A subprocess that decided would be a second accepting party. Reached through the loop as well as straight through: SF_UA_8 re-enters at A_Impact, so a run where the reviewer found something fixable arrives here a second time with different evidence. That is a genuine re-analysis and its op="note" appends rather than deduping, which is the behaviour wanted — a second note records that the options were weighed again against changed inputs. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to absorb the impact candidate, extracted On the edge OUT of Task_AssessImpact and before Task_CommitPush, because the impact assessment is the evidence the options are weighed against. An analysis before it would compare ways of absorbing a downstream effect nobody has measured yet; one after the commit would be a rationalisation of a choice already pushed. Not between Task_AssessImpact and Task_ReviewImpact: those are in different processes with no sequence flow between them; the assessment reaches the committee through Task_CompareBeforeAfter. In the Agent lane, matching upstream-version-adoption: this step produces the options and their trade-offs, and GW_Approved in the committee review is where a decision is taken. On the trigger: reaching this call is not the same as running the whole of it. Process_OptionsAnalysis opens with A_Frame, whose trigger is opening-brief's — irreversibility and surprise, not size — and leaving at that first activity is a correct outcome rather than a skipped step. A copy-edit exits immediately; a logic change that moves an indicator (from Task_EditLogic) does not. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/content-change-review-make.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis . Options analysis how to implement candidate, extracted On the single edge from Start_Process_CRDM_Deliver into A_Implement, so the approach is chosen before any code exists. The three loop-backs into A_Implement — _5 (increment rejected), _7 (MVP not ready), _13 (feedback translated) — deliberately BYPASS this call. Routing them through it would run the subprocess on every iteration of the inner loop, which is the ceremony this design refuses: a gate invoked on every pass stops being read. An iteration reworks an approach already chosen; if the APPROACH is what is wrong, that is not a loop iteration and it belongs to the calling step in crdm-requirements.bpmn. Contrast upstream-version-adoption, where the loop DOES re-enter the analysis. There the loop-back returns to A_Impact, which re-gathers the evidence, so the second pass weighs genuinely different inputs. Here the loop returns to implementation with the evidence unchanged. A_Implement carries a note on the bean (its claim is the OPEN that Process_CRDM calls first); this step carries no bean op, because Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note on the bean the caller claimed. 500a3b326382.content: Package with digests candidate, extracted The serialization alone is not a package. Each one links back to the library entry and to the section it came from. WHY IN INGESTION AND NOT LATER. A statement nobody can read beside its source is reviewed from memory, or not at all. Publishing when the entry is promoted means a reviewer can check every extracted statement against its source the moment it exists. The sub-process is the same for every content type. The content type decides only how its pages look, through its adapter. An entry that yields no statements (a referenced source, a dataset) passes through it with nothing to publish, and says so. Process_RenderKgToCdn, entered with the tree Task_Build rendered, branches/<slug>/ under the site root as the publication root URL, and GitHub Pages as the target, so its gh-pages Tool pushes. For this target the push is keep_files: true with a destination_dir, so it adds one directory beside whatever else is on the branch; it is also RETRIED once: five other workflows push to gh-pages without joining this one's concurrency group, and a queue does not help because GitHub CANCELS a pending job when a newer one arrives for the same group rather than queueing it. Measured 2026-09-19: three staging runs from three different branches inside 17 seconds, two cancelled. The call returns the push's status and message; the render log and the PR comment that follow are this process's own. THE PREVIEW CAP rides in the same commit (owner ruling 2026-10-02, issue #1868: "cap the maximum number of previews (<= 10) and rotate old ones off", amended 2026-10-04 to a SIZE budget: "Cap by size, not count", "3gb"): staging-rotate.ts keeps this preview plus the most recently updated others while their total fits MAX_PREVIEW_BYTES = 3 GB and removes the rest, oldest first, each with a removed render-log entry and its record retired into branches/_retired/. Every push attempt re-reads gh-pages and re-decides rather than rebasing, so a lost race never pushes a stale removal. A rotated-off preview is regenerated by the next push to its PR branch.
