4823c4028600.title: Q
4823c4028600.content: QA gate: check dispositions against the people and the pull request candidate, extracted Before Ready for merge. Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, the PR's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every comment number has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted comment has its change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate or Out of scope one has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set), first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows both under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/collab/processes/content/public-comment-change.bpmn#Task_QaGate . QA gate: check dispositions and PR candidate, extracted Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), the people's Blue Disposition and feedback, the pull request's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every feedback item has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted item has the change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope item has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set) on the Agent tab, first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows the gate under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. QA working copy, built once (NOT A GATE) candidate, extracted Bean jtfk, issue #2456. bun run qa:working-copy (bean 72a8) — the bootstrap kg-export, then every declared QA writer — used to run INSIDE each job that reads the QA tree, and qa-publish ran the same writers again: nine builds of one tree from one commit, measured at 2,284 of 4,714 runner-seconds (48 %) on run 37659324493. Now the qa-working-copy job builds it once and uploads everything the build changed as an artifact with a sha256 manifest; each reader downloads it, checks the manifest against the hash this job reported and every restored file against the manifest, and only then judges. An artifact rather than a cache, because a cache key built from less than the real inputs serves stale data; an artifact is per run and exact. It judges nothing, so it is not a gate and does not reach GW_Join; a failed build fails every reader at its first step (they run if: !cancelled()), never a skip. Drawn feeding GW_Readers, the four tasks that wait for it; within them typescript-static and gates-standalone read no QA tree and do not wait, and qa-publish waits for it as well as for Task_RepositoryGates. fcb0b345a4c9.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 639 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 56 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 229 (SKOS). Split by first letter. 969 terms are too many for one page within its budget of 1.0 MB, so they are on 3 pages by the first letter of the label. The ranges are fixed, so a term’s address does not move as terms are added. A label that does not start with a letter is on the first page. | A–D: 294 terms | E–Q: 308 terms | R–Z: 367 terms | .

df257caa1c31.title: Already somebody else’s concept?
df257caa1c31.content: Extracted candidates are minted from this repository’s own assets and are not, by themselves, checked against any vocabulary. check:term-mapping asks whether each already exists as a concept somebody is authoritative for — SKOS for what a term MEANS, FHIR for a clinical code’s operational semantics — and the two are separate questions with separate answers. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 4271 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 4271 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin.
